subject: FinApps: sudden 95th pct latency and reserved capacity shortfall
messages:
From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@finapps.io>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden errors and latency on production (FinApps)

Hi Stephanie —

We're seeing a sharp increase in 503s and 95th percentile latency for the /generate endpoint from our prod tenant starting ~08:45 PDT. Error rate jumped from ~0.5% to ~6% and many of our payment flows are timing out. This is impacting a set of merchants.

We've attached a short perf trace and a couple of sample request IDs (trace files attached). Can you confirm whether our reserved pool is saturated or if this looks like a model/regression issue? We need an ETA for mitigation.

Sample request IDs: req_6a2b, req_6a33, req_6a47

Thanks,
Tom
Director, Platform Ops
FinApps Inc.

Forwarding Tom's note — marking as P1 for Dedicated reserved capacity impacts.

Immediate steps I'm asking for:
- Vivek: run pool observer and confirm per-gpu utilization and queue lengths for tenant finapps_prod (priority tagging).
- Jordan: reach out to FinApps exec ops (Priya) to set expectations while we triage.
- Stephanie: pull any SLO credit history and existing compensation commitments.

If we confirm reserved capacity saturation, we should propose a temporary routing fallback to hosted lower-latency replicas AND start an emergency add of +2 GPU capacity to the customer's reserved pool (subject to approval). I want an owner for the approval path now.

Marissa
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: FinApps perf incident — pool metrics & recommended mitigation

I'm seeing clear evidence of pool saturation: GPUs in pool finapps-prod-1 are at sustained 98–100% SM utilization and queue depth has hit >300 waiting requests. The load pattern shifted at 08:46 GMT-7 — traffic fanout increased from a handful of clients to a wide cohort (likely a campaign). Attached trace matches KV-cache misses on hot prefixes, increasing per-token work.

Short-term mitigations we can execute immediately (10–30m):
- Activate per-tenant throttling at the load-balancer replacing token-based burst limits with request-rate caps to preserve latency for in-flight critical flows (we can set a rule to favor /payments/* endpoints).
- Spin up +2 GPU emergency nodes into the reserved pool (will increase throughput; provisioning ETA ~14 minutes if we use hot-standby capacity in us-west2).
- Fallback: route best-effort traffic to hosted replicas (lossy but keeps critical flows alive).

Longer-term action items:
- Rebalance model shards — current shard allocation gives finapps_prod uneven work distribution for long-context requests.
- Recommend permanent +1 reserved GPU commit for daytime campaign windows and implement autoscale policy for predictable bursts.

I'll start the emergency spin-up and push LB throttling rule now. Jordan/Marissa: who has approval to accept a short-term charge for emergency capacity? We should also prepare a credit proposal given SLA impact.

Vivek
Sr. Infra Engineer — Serving Runtime

Attachments: finapps_perf_trace_0315.zip (same as customer attachment, sanitized)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finapps.io>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@finapps.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, procurement@finapps.io
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2026 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Status update and mitigation plan — FinApps production impact (P1)

Hi Priya / Tom —

Thanks again for the quick flag earlier. Summary and next steps:

What happened: at ~08:46 PDT a FinApps campaign caused a volume fanout that produced sustained hot-prefix KV-cache misses and pushed the dedicated pool (finapps-prod-1) to saturation. This increased queueing and raised the 95th percentile latency and 503s.

What we did (completed):
- Activated request-rate caps to protect critical /payments endpoints (applied at 09:05 PDT).
- Provisioned +2 emergency GPUs into the reserved pool; nodes came online by 09:22 PDT and reduced queue depth by ~70%.
- Enabled temporary routing of non-critical traffic to hosted replicas (keeps user flows alive while preserving customer data isolation for critical flows).

Impact: error rates reduced from ~6% to ~1.1%; 95th pct latency is trending down but not fully back to baseline for long-context requests.

Next steps (we propose — timelines in parentheses):
- Permanent shard rebalance and autoscale policy for finapps_prod (1–2 business days to validate, deploy next maintenance window).
- Recommend increasing committed reserved capacity by +1 GPU during peak campaign windows (we will provide a cost estimate and projected latency improvement by tomorrow EOD).
- Compensation: we've prepared a provisional SLA credit proposal for the period of elevated errors; see attached PDF.

We own the technical remediation and will coordinate an after-action review. Marissa/Jordan will follow up on procurement/contract language and credit acceptance.

If you approve the temporary commit (+2 emergency GPUs already provisioned for immediate relief) we'll finalize billing/credit reconciliation with procurement.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this is high-impact and are treating as priority. I'll set up a quick 30-minute bridge at 10:00 PDT tomorrow to walk through the permanent plan unless you ask for earlier.

— Stephanie Nguyen
Senior AE, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed_credit_and_timeline.pdf
